function.name: qb_garch_volatility
function.description: Real GARCH(1,1) fits computed on the Jetson. A MISSING fit is reported explicitly, never as zero volatility — the engine drops non-stationary fits (alpha+beta>=1) and any pair/timeframe with fewer than 100 observations. Intraday fits are the least trustworthy: plain GARCH misreads FX session seasonality as volatility clustering.

function.name: qb_markov_regime
function.description: Empirical regime-transition matrix from the Jetson's live HMM classifiers. ALWAYS picks one vocabulary: 'directional_v1' (BULL/BEAR/SIDEWAYS, from markov_minion) or 'volatility_phase_v1' (EXPANSION/COMPRESSION/EXHAUSTION, from deep_hmm_regime). The two are orthogonal axes and must never be pooled — a BULL->EXPANSION 'transition' is two classifiers disagreeing, not a state change.

function.name: qb_seasonal_bias
function.description: Two different things, deliberately separated. seasonal_deviation is FULL-SAMPLE (it has lookahead) and is for RANKING pairs by |z_score| only. latestPointInTimeBias comes from seasonal_bias_asof, which uses only years strictly before the target — that is the one safe to join per-bar. A NULL bias score means too few prior years to say, never 'no seasonal bias'.

function.name: qb_key_levels
function.description: Dealer PDH/PDL/PDM/PWH/PWL and 20D range, gamma strikes and session anchors/sigma targets for a pair, with distance in pips from the latest closed bar. Needs NO chart. session='next' (default) computes dealer levels for the NEXT trading session on the NY-weekday convention, so over a weekend PDH/PDL are Friday's — which is what you want for Monday. session='jetson' instead returns the Jetson's own dealers_levels row as served, whose weekend rows count as sessions. Pass include_pine to also get a ready-to-paste Pine v6 indicator.

as_of.description: ISO timestamp — compute levels as they stood then.

datasets.description: Limit to some of: dealers_levels, gamma_levels, session_ranges.

function.name: qb_monte_carlo_forecast
function.description: Resamples the pair's REAL historical hourly returns with replacement rather than assuming lognormal/GBM, so the fan carries the pair's actual fat tails and skew. Returns quantile bands per horizon bar. The fan starts from ml_ready's latest close, which over a weekend is Friday's.

function.name: qb_signal_significance_test
function.description: Does a signal actually predict the anti-lookahead forward return in walk_forward_labels, or is the apparent edge indistinguishable from randomly shuffled labels? Uses an as-of join (a label only ever sees a signal known at or before it), keeps ONLY non-overlapping forward windows so one price move cannot be counted many times, and refuses to produce a p-value when the sample is too thin.

function.name: qb_model_scoreboard
function.description: Scores the Jetson's time-series models (river, kronos, hmm) against its own naive persistence baseline on the same predictions, with an exact McNemar test and Wilson CIs. Counts ONLY non-overlapping prediction windows by default — pooling overlapping ones inflates n and makes edges appear that are not there. Benjamini-Hochberg q-values are reported across all groups: treat a verdict as a finding only when survivesFdr is true.

function.name: qb_trevo_survivors
function.description: Survivors of the weekly genetic search over boolean feature trees. train/oos Sharpe are the GA's OWN numbers — its in-house gate, NOT an independent verdict (use lean_validation for that). vetoedByNullTest flags a survivor whose train Sharpe failed to beat 3x a shuffled null. A run with zero survivors writes no rows here at all.

function.name: qb_lean_validation
function.description: ADVISORY only — nothing here gates execution. LEAN walks a survivor's own fire array bar-by-bar through a strictly-causal engine over a hold-out the GA never trained on, so a disagreement is about the ENGINE, not a re-implementation. zeroSpreadBacktest is TRUE: prices are bid==ask==mid, so leanSharpe is evidence about point-in-time correctness, NOT about paying costs. Judge on leanSharpe vs gaOosSharpe, never on net profit. ok=false rows are refusals, not zeros.

function.name: qb_query_sql
function.description: Runs one read-only SQL statement over Jetson datasets loaded into an in-memory DuckDB. Use DATASET NAMES as table names (e.g. SELECT * FROM candles_1h LIMIT 5); market_bars is an alias for candles_1h. Each table holds at most the newest `rows_per_dataset` rows for the pair you pass — raise it to reach further back. Datasets keyed by CURRENCY get both legs of the pair. Time functions run in UTC.

pair.description: Required when any referenced dataset is filtered by pair or currency.

datasets.description: Extra datasets to load that the SQL text does not name literally.

since.description: ISO date lower bound passed to the datasets that accept it.

function.name: qb_provide_ai_context
function.description: Builds compact markdown describing a pair's CURRENT state from the live Jetson, grouped by the source notes in sources/ (price, volatility, levels, positioning, momentum, regime, confluence, seasonality, calendar). Every dataset shows its as-of time and age, so stale data is visible rather than read as current. Validation datasets (forward returns) are never included.

groups.description: Limit to some source groups (see source_graph).

function.name: qb_live_bars
function.description: Recent bars from the live tick pipeline. Crosses are synthesized from two majors, not observed quotes.

function.name: qb_live_pairs
function.description: The pairs the live tick pipeline carries, split into real IG majors and synthesized crosses, with per-file age. Age is file mtime and the daemon rewrites files even when no new ticks land — so a fresh age proves the writer is alive, NOT that data is flowing.

function.name: qb_source_graph
function.description: The dataset registry built from the markdown notes in sources/: which groups exist, which datasets each contains, what each feeds, and — checked against the live Jetson catalog — which are actually served, how old they are, and which notes reference datasets that no longer exist.

force.description: Write the markdown even when the Jetson is unreachable.

function.name: qb_chainlog_query
function.description: Search the shared append-only research record that Gemini CLI, Claude and Colab jobs all write to. Filter by agent, entry kind (hypothesis/run/result/verdict/correction/note), verdict or free text. Start here before proposing an experiment — it is how you find out the question was already answered, or answered and then corrected.

verbose.description: Full entry bodies. Default false returns one line per entry. Bodies here run to thousands of characters and an agent re-sends every tool result on each subsequent step, so ask for them only when you need them.

grep.description: Free-text match over the whole entry.

function.name: qb_registry_show
function.description: Every recorded test of one feature, plus the chainlog entry each cites. If a row's chainlog_ref does not resolve it is reported as a dangling reference — that row's method is not on the record and it should not be trusted.

function.name: qb_mcl_compute_wilson_ci
function.description: Asymmetric binomial confidence interval for wins/total. Use this rather than the normal approximation, which is the one people reach for and which breaks exactly where it matters: at small n, or when the rate is near 0 or 1, it produces intervals that run past [0,1] and under-cover. Reports n<30 as provisional. Note the interval assumes INDEPENDENT trials — if your trials are overlapping windows or correlated pairs, n is not what you think and the interval is too tight regardless of which formula you use.

function.name: qb_mcl_discretize_feature
function.description: Bins a feature into k buckets using ONLY data available at each bar. QUANTILE_ROLLING takes the quantile of a trailing window; VOLATILITY_NORMALIZED divides by trailing ATR first. The distinction that matters: binning on full-sample quantiles — which is what pandas.qcut over a whole column does — leaks the future into every early bar, because the bin edges were computed from data that had not happened yet. Bars before the window fills are returned as bin null, never forced into a bucket.

function.name: qb_mcl_anchor_event
function.description: Locates discrete session transitions — LONDON_OPEN (08:00 UTC), US_ORB_1000 (10:00 New York) and NY_MIDNIGHT — and returns the bar at each, with the range that followed. Anchors are the FX session grid, so they respect the 17:00 New York roll: Friday ends at the close and Sunday evening counts toward Monday. Weekend bars carry no session and are excluded rather than silently bucketed into the wrong day.

orb_minutes.description: Range window after the anchor, default 60.
